reason: scratch_lifetime ranks first because it directly targets per-call scratch allocation with the smallest kernel change and low correctness risk, though alignment benefit is unverified and it does not reduce scratch size or initialization. tail_alignment and compiler_codegen are narrow, low-risk checks; the latter should begin with assembly inspection. Address and register scheduling experiments change little and preserve arithmetic order. K unrolling and transpose or layout changes have greater code, tail, or memory risks. Packing adds allocation and traffic; prior noisy outcomes do not establish causality, so they rank last.
